data.content:
## The same vault, one era earlier - P2SH

Before taproot, all four spending paths live in **one script**, glued together with IF/ELSE ladders. The spender steers the branches by pushing 1/0 flags:

```
OP_IF
    <Alice> OP_CHECKSIG                        ← path 1: daily spending
OP_ELSE
    OP_IF
        <144> OP_CSV OP_DROP                   ← path 2: Bob, ~1 day
        <Bob> OP_CHECKSIG
    OP_ELSE
        OP_IF
            <4320> OP_CSV OP_DROP              ← path 3: Charlie, ~30 days
            <Charlie> OP_CHECKSIG
        OP_ELSE
            <8640> OP_CSV OP_DROP              ← path 4: estate council, ~60 days
            OP_2 <Bob> <Charlie> <Diana> OP_3
            OP_CHECKMULTISIG
        OP_ENDIF
    OP_ENDIF
OP_ENDIF
```

Roughly 235 bytes, wrapped in the usual 23-byte P2SH envelope: `OP_HASH160 <hash> OP_EQUAL`.

**Hidden only until the first spend.** The address is a hash, so the vault starts out private - but the *first* spend of any path publishes the entire script forever: every heir's key, every delay, the whole family structure. Taproot's tree reveals one leaf per spend and nothing else - and the key path reveals no script at all.

**Everyone pays for every branch.** Each spend - including Alice's Tuesday coffee - must carry all 235 bytes plus the steering flags on-chain. In the taproot version Alice's daily spend is a 66-byte witness that looks identical to any single-sig payment; the contingency paths cost bytes only in the year they actually fire.

**Control flow is where script bugs live.** Three nested IF/ELSE/ENDIF ladders, flag ordering the spender must get right, a DROP after every CSV. The taproot tree replaces control flow with *structure*: each leaf is a short, straight-line script, and the merkle proof does the branching.

data.content:
## The same vault in taproot - a tree instead of a ladder

The four paths stop being one script. Three become **separate straight-line scripts**, each a leaf in a tree; the fourth becomes no script at all:

```
        Q = P_Alice + H_TapTweak(P ‖ root)·G     ← the whole lock: OP_1 <Q>
        │
      root
     /    \
 branch    leaf C
 /    \
leaf A  leaf B

leaf A:  <144>  OP_CSV OP_DROP  <Bob>     OP_CHECKSIG
leaf B:  <4320> OP_CSV OP_DROP  <Charlie> OP_CHECKSIG
leaf C:  <8640> OP_CSV OP_DROP
         <Bob> OP_CHECKSIG  <Charlie> OP_CHECKSIGADD  <Diana> OP_CHECKSIGADD
         OP_2 OP_NUMEQUAL
```

**Path 1 is not a leaf - it's the key.** Alice is the internal key P, so her daily spend is the 66-byte key-path witness from the intro flow. No script surfaces, no tree is mentioned; the chain sees an ordinary single-sig payment. The vault's most-used path costs nothing extra, ever.

**No steering flags, no ladder.** "Which branch" is no longer opcodes the spender executes - it's a merkle proof the spender *presents*. Each leaf is short, linear, and independently auditable: ~40 bytes for A and B, ~110 for the council leaf, versus the 235-byte monolith. The IF/ELSE bug surface is simply gone.

**One spend reveals one leaf.** When Bob recovers after a day, the chain learns his script and a control block - parity byte, Alice's internal key, and the two sibling hashes proving his leaf was always inside Q (33 + 2×32 = 97 bytes). Leaf B and leaf C stay 32-byte hashes forever: Charlie's delay, the council's existence, even *how many* other clauses there were - never published. The estate leaf, one level shallower, would need only a 65-byte proof.

**And the multisig modernized on the way in:** OP_CHECKMULTISIG is disabled in tapscript - the council leaf counts valid signatures instead (`OP_CHECKSIG / OP_CHECKSIGADD ... OP_2 OP_NUMEQUAL`), one slot per key, empty slot for non-signers, no dummy element. Bob and Charlie appear in the council under **fresh keys** - deliberately. A revealed leaf publishes its key, and a reused key would let observers grind guesses against the hidden sibling hashes. Roles repeat; keys never do.

data.content:
# Overview - The Other Door

Most contracts end in agreement - that was the intro flow's bet, and its key path cashed it: one signature, nothing revealed. **This flow is what happens when they don't.**

Alice's vault (told in the two story cards) guards the coins: her key is the internal key P, and three timelocked recovery clauses hang in the tree beneath it - Bob after ~a day, Charlie after ~a month, a 2-of-3 council after ~two months. In this run, Alice never shows up. Bob recovers the coins.

Two transactions live on this canvas:

- **TX1 builds the vault**: a key-path spend of a faucet coin into `OP_1 <Q>`, where Q commits to Alice's key *and* the three-leaf tree - the tweak node's merkle-root input is finally non-empty
- **TX2 is Bob's recovery**: it waits out the 144-block CSV, then opens leaf A with a three-item witness - his signature, the leaf script itself, and the proof it was always inside Q

Leaf B and leaf C are committed alternatives - hashed into Q, never spent here.

Everything is built live: leaf hashes, branch hashes, the control block, the extended sighash.

*Builds on Taproot intro - tweak, TapSighash and the key path are assumed.*
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## TapLeaf and TapBranch - hashing a tree

Every leaf becomes 32 bytes the same way:

```
leaf hash = tagged_hash("TapLeaf", c0 ‖ compact_size(script) ‖ script)
```

`c0` is the leaf *version* - tapscript v0 today, an upgrade lane for tomorrow: every leaf could speak a different script language. Each leaf group builds this preimage from parts - version, length, script - through the TapLeaf tag machinery.

Pairs then merge upward:

```
branch = tagged_hash("TapBranch", min(h₁,h₂) ‖ max(h₁,h₂))
```

The sort is the quiet masterstroke: children hash in **lexicographic order**, so a merkle proof never needs left/right directions - the verifier sorts too, and any path is just a bare list of sibling hashes. The Tree Builder pairs A with B, then their branch with C, and its output lands in the tweak node's second input. Empty in the intro, load-bearing here: Q now commits to Alice's key *and* every clause beneath it.
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## The control block - the proof half of the reveal Bob's witness must convince a verifier of something the chain has never seen: that his script was inside Q from the start. The control block is that proof: ``` c0 leaf version ‖ parity of Q (1 byte)

Alice's internal key (32 bytes) sibling hashes, leaf → root (32 each) ``` The verifier replays the build: hash Bob's script into a TapLeaf, fold in the siblings (sorting each pair), tweak P by the resulting root - and compare against the Q sitting in the spent output. Match, and the commitment is proven; then, and only then, the script executes. Two promises from earlier flows get paid here. The **parity bit** the intro parked: during verification Q is a full point again, and this bit says which of its two y-values to lift - `c0` even, `c1` odd. And the **internal key P** finally surfaces - exactly as the tweak card warned it would in a script-path spend. What still doesn't surface: leaf B and leaf C. Charlie's clause, the council's existence, even the count of other doors - sibling hashes forever.
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## The script-path sighash - and the witness that carries it

Three things change against the intro's key-path signing:

**`spend_type` flips to `02`** - script path, no annex - and the message grows a tail after `input_index`:

```
tapleaf_hash   which clause this signature serves
00             key version (script keys - not the c0 leaf version)
ffffffff       last OP_CODESEPARATOR position (none)
```

The leaf hash inside the signature pins it to *this* clause: Bob's signature cannot be replayed into some other leaf that happens to contain his key.

**`nSequence` carries the timelock**: `90000000` = 144 blocks, BIP-68 encoded. OP_CSV in the script only *compares* against this field - consensus enforces the actual age. The script demands the promise, the transaction makes it, the chain checks it.

**The signing key is Bob's, raw.** No tweak - tweaking belongs to the key path. Inside a leaf, keys are plain BIP340 x-only keys, and CHECKSIG verifies against them directly.

The witness then stacks the only three things a script-path spend ever needs:

```
40 <signature>       what the leaf demands
27 <leaf script>     the clause itself
61 <control block>   the proof it was committed
```

66 bytes bought the key path; Bob's unhappy path costs ~200.
data.title: Text Info Node

data.content:
## Try it yourself - recover as the council

Rebuild TX2 through **leaf C**: the 2-of-3 council claims the vault. Hints for what taproot changes:

- **Signatures are counted.** CHECKSIGADD gives each key a slot; the counter must land *exactly* on `OP_2`.
- **The skip is an empty item.** The non-signer's slot stays in the witness as a zero-length element - a wrong signature there doesn't add 0, it kills the script. No `OP_0` dummy anywhere.
- **Witness order is script order, reversed:** Diana, Charlie, Bob.
- **The proof shrinks.** One level up the tree, the merkle path is a single sibling - `Branch(A,B)` - and the control block drops to 65 bytes. Sequence: `8640`.
data.title: Text Info Node
